This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

VU Computer Science combines programming and software engineering with algorithms, formal reasoning, mathematics, computer systems, networks, data and AI. Its general bachelor includes constrained second-year options, an open academic semester and a supervised scientific CS project.

UCR offers two qualified responses: computer systems, software and algorithms; and mathematical computing and intelligent systems. Both contain substantial actual computing and mathematical methods. The first retains more software-development and advanced-algorithm study; the second adds linear systems, calculus and robotic motion planning. These programmes have important gaps in dedicated hardware, web/security engineering, formal computation and the VU project sequence. Complementary design, cognition and communication courses do not remove those gaps.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: General Computer Science; three selected constrained choices

The general 2026–2027 route contains60EC compulsory Year1,45EC compulsory plus15EC constrained choices Year2, and30EC prescribed Year3 plus30EC open academic study. Academic Writing3EC, Computer Security6EC and HCI6EC are shown as selected choices, not compulsory for everyone. There is no formal specialization. Object-Oriented and Functional Programming and Operating Systems require prior Computer Programming or Systems Programming Project (the TER also specifies an approved earlier programming pair for the former). Project entry requires at least120EC of the Computer Science bachelor. The project normally spans periods5–6; semester1 is possible through the coordinator. Students arrange a topic and supervisor before starting. Internships require prior approval of a VU staff examiner. Individual or group projects have distinct student roles and individual assessment by two examiners: technical contribution50%, thesis40%, oral presentation10%, each at least5.5. The supervisor must submit the graded thesis/form by31July for August graduation or31January for February graduation. Generative AI is allowed only for orientation/brainstorming, not final-submission content. English diagnostic testing and the required refresher are mandatory without extra EC. BSA ordinarily requires42EC first-year credits, subject to exceptions. Practical/tutorial attendance follows unit manuals; thesis/placement regulations apply. Individual open choices need prior board approval, at least12EC at level300 and at most6EC at level100. Abroad, at most one6EC master unit may be included and cannot be reused later. Eligible university/listed minors can be taken without prior board approval; the general Data Science and Basics of AI university minors are excluded for CS students. The CS-specific Business Analytics and Data Science minor remains eligible. No elective minors are stacked.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Computer Science at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with 2 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Computer systems, software and algorithms

Builds a substantial computing programme around Python programming, networks and operating systems, relational databases, C++ and functional software development, algorithms, discrete mathematics, statistics and AI methods. Product-design work contributes customer-needs analysis and prototyping, while philosophy, rhetoric and ethics develop critical argument and responsible practice. Those complementary subjects do not replace dedicated hardware, security, web engineering or the VU independent research project.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Mathematical computing and intelligent systems

Prioritizes mathematical computing and autonomous systems: linear algebra, numerical computation, linear-system transforms, calculus, statistics, machine learning, optimisation, vision and robotic motion planning. Programming, networks and databases remain substantial foundations. Introductory brain and behaviour supplies human cognition and research-method context for responsible AI; it does not implement human–computer interaction design. This direction trades software-development and advanced-algorithm depth for mathematical models and robotics.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

VU requires computer organization, web technology, smart systems engineering, systems programming, automata and complexity, and a supervised 15 EC CS project. The selected VU options add HCI and security. UCR has substantial programming, algorithms, systems, mathematics and AI, but leaves important specialist gaps. Product design and human cognition are complementary foundations, not replacements for these components.

The VU project requires a scientific question, literature, systematic investigation, a thesis and oral presentation. Individual or group projects are assessed individually by two examiners. UCR course projects do not automatically supply that independent research requirement; optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Consumer Product Design
You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
Close

AI Ethics
AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, accountability, the moral status of AI systems and broader political risks. Students also consider trust and decision-making, empathy and confidentiality in clinical settings, algorithmic stereotypes, and how AI companions and tutors may affect children’s learning and relationships.
Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Logic & Discrete Mathematics
Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
Close

Optimization Methods in AI
Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction. Laboratory exercises and projects include graph search, convex optimisation, and linear and nonlinear programming.
Close

Reinforcement Learning
Explores reinforcement learning. Covers theoretical frameworks and algorithms and requires students to implement algorithms and build agents using neural networks that learn through trial and error.
Close

Networks & Operating Systems
Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.
Close

Database Management Systems
Introduces relational database management systems and SQL. Covers relational database theory, authorization, normalization and query processing.
Close

Software Development
Covers software design, creation, testing and maintenance. Uses C++ and Haskell and covers planning, requirements gathering, testing, deployment and maintenance through discussions and code reviews.
Close

Algorithms & Data Structures
Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
Close

Advanced Algorithms
Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Robotics
Covers computational problems in robotics. Includes forward and inverse kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and robotic grasping and manipulation.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Linear Algebra
Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and applications including Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains.
Close

Computational & Numerical Methods
Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.
Close

Advanced Calculus
Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.
Close

Linear Systems
Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.
Close

Probability & Statistics
Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
Close

Introduction to Western Philosophy
Introduces central themes from Western philosophy over 2,500 years. Encourages inquiry into the significance of philosophical issues and their relation to other disciplines and teaches theoretical methods used by philosophers.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close
